corrections.previousValue:
Risshaku-ji (山寺) is reached by a direct ≈20-minute Senzan Line train from Yamagata. Admission is {{fact:yamadera-admission-500-yen}}, cash only.

There is no cable car, ropeway, or shortcut anywhere on the mountain — the only way up to the Godaido viewing platform and Okunoin is on foot, via roughly 1,015 stone steps (figures vary 1,015-1,070 depending on the source), and there are no ramps or elevators anywhere on the site, including at the base.

Konponchudo, the main hall about 3 minutes' walk from the base entrance, is a genuinely worthwhile stop on its own without climbing further — the honest option for anyone who'd rather not attempt the stairs.

Lunch: Takifudo Namasoba, ≈7 min from the station near the mountain entrance, open 11:00-15:30. ⚠ Its seat counts appear only in restaurant directories, so phone 023-695-2039 ahead to hold a table for 8.

10:00-14:00 is when tour groups arrive and the paths and Godaido platform get genuinely crowded, worse still once koyo (autumn foliage) season builds — which is also the window the soba shop opens into. Climb early, eat after.

Taimenseki, right at the station, is a smaller, quicker soba stop for anyone splitting off from the group lunch or catching an earlier train.

corrections.previousValue: A Taisho-era wooden ryokan street along the Ginzan River, gas lamps lighting ≈16:30-17:00 (seasonal — the schedule shifts earlier as sunset comes sooner through October), plus the riverside "Waraku" foot bath and Shirogane Falls (22m) at the street's end. corrections.previousValue:
Morning: Bunshokan (free, 9:00-16:30, with a rear wheelchair entrance, 10 loaner wheelchairs and a stair lift — the one city sight whose access is documented) or Yamagata Marugoto-kan Beninokura, a restored Edo-era merchant warehouse compound paired with Soba Sanbyakubou's 30-seat private room for lunch.

Withdraw cash before leaving the city — Ginzan Onsen has no ATM or convenience store. From Yamagata Station, take the JR Ōu Line to Oishida (≈50 min local / ≈28 min Tsubasa), then the Hanagasa Bus to Ginzan Onsen: {{fact:hanagasa-bus-fare-1000-yen}}, ≈35-40 minutes, no reservation needed, and only a handful of departures a day — the operator runs a different timetable per season, so read the April–October one. Board with the group's luggage in good time; missing a bus can mean waiting over two hours for the next.

Check into Ginzanso (the largest property in town, best odds of hosting all 8 together) and see the street's gas lamps light ≈16:30-17:00 (seasonal — earlier as October's sunset comes sooner), best photo window 16:30-17:30.

corrections.previousValue:
Emergency numbers: police 110, ambulance/fire 119 — both free, nationwide, with English-speaking operators available.

Yamagata city has ordinary drugstore chains (Tsuruha Drug is common across Tohoku) for over-the-counter needs; English support is basic, not fluent medical consultation. Ginzan Onsen and Yamadera have no pharmacy — bring what the group needs for those days.

⚠ Routine vaccinations, MMR included, should be current before departure — check your own doctor or national health authority for Japan's current recommendations.
corrections.correctedValue:

Yamagata city has the usual national drugstore chains (Matsumoto Kiyoshi, Cocokara Fine, Sun Drug) for over-the-counter needs; English support is basic, not fluent medical consultation. Ginzan Onsen and Yamadera have no pharmacy — bring what the group needs for those days.

⚠ Routine vaccinations, MMR included, should be current before departure — check your own doctor or national health authority for Japan's current recommendations.
corrections.claim: The section's sole citation names Matsumoto Kiyoshi, Cocokara Fine and Sun Drug as the drugstore chains, and contains nothing about the 110/119 emergency lines, English-speaking operators, or Tsuruha Drug
